newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy economy weak but some positive signs - Isco.
newsitem.headline: Italy economy weak but some positive signs - Isco.

text.p: The Italian economy remains weak but there are positive signs on the inflation front which give hope for a more lasting fall in interest rates, state research body Isco said in its latest monthly report.

"The Italian economy has continued to be characterised by a phase of weakness," Isco said, citing unsatisfactory domestic demand, an inversion in investment trends and a more limited growth in exports.
"But on the other hand, positive signals have continued to be seen on the inflationary front," it said.
August annual consumer price inflation fell to 3.4 percent from 3.6 percent in July, a seventh consecutive fall.

"In the absence of tensions on the international financial markets, the more restrained dynamic of price expectations should have a lasting effect on the process of falling interest rates which was interupted in summer," Isco said.
The Bank of Italy made a long-awaited move to cut its key discount rate in July, lowering to 8.25 percent the rate which had remained at 9.0 percent for over a year.

Isco added that "encouraging signals in this direction have also emerged from the monetary authorities" in its control of money market liquidity, which analysts noted has recently seemed to have been managed in a less tight manner.
